title: Payout Methods Dormancy, Returned Transfer and Deficit Recovery Terms
content:
Payout Methods place an active method on hold as dormant after a rail-specific number of calendar days without a transfer. The handling of a returned transfer, reactivation, and the recovery of amounts a host owes follow terms that are the same on every rail.

## Dormancy period by rail

| Rail | Calendar days without a transfer after which an active method is placed on hold as dormant |
|---|---|
| Direct Deposit (ACH) | 365 |
| Fast Pay Debit Card | 365 |
| PayPal | 365 |
| Payoneer | 365 |
| International Wire Transfer | 180 |
| Western Union Cash Pickup | 180 |

## Terms common to every rail

| Item | Every rail |
|---|---|
| When a transfer is returned | The amount is re-credited to the undisbursed balance and the method is placed on hold |
| What is needed before a method on hold is reactivated | Updated account details re-verified after the hold |
| How amounts owed by the host are recovered | Deducted from the next released earnings on any of the host's payout methods, oldest deficit first |
| When an unrecovered deficit leaves support's hands for collections | After 90 calendar days |

## Points of reference

- International Wire Transfer and Western Union Cash Pickup go dormant after 180 days; the four other rails after 365 days.
- Recovery of an amount owed is not limited to the method the amount arose on: it reaches the next released earnings on **any** of the host's payout methods, the oldest deficit first.

**Hypothetical reading.** An imagined International Wire Transfer method last paid 180 calendar days ago has reached its dormancy period; an imagined PayPal method last paid the same day has not, as its period is 365 days.
